title: Docs operations: SDK sample matrix, golden-playback, and canonical-fix runbook
author: Aisha Banerjee
body:
Summary

This runbook defines the operational process, validation matrix, and canonical fix patterns for SDK example code and API example snippets that appear in Redwood Inference developer documentation. Its goal is to make docs-first SDK regressions reproducible and fast to remediate, reduce support noise, and guarantee reproducible "golden" outputs for automated checks.

Scope

- Applies to all SDK example repositories and docs-site snippets owned by eng-developer-experience.
- Covers languages: python, typescript, go, java, and curl/CLI examples.
- Includes local validation, CI gating, rollback/hotfix, and support-canonicalization steps.

Roles & ownership

1) Docs owner (primary): eng-developer-experience docs team (Aisha Banerjee) – responsible for snippet correctness and publishing checklist.
2) SDK maintainers (secondary): language SDK teams – responsible for runtime/behavior regressions in examples.
3) Support triage owner: customer-success (primary contact for escalations).

SLOs & validation thresholds

- Docs CI green rate: 99% on main branch for snippet execution.
- Golden playback match: 95% token/field-level match for deterministic snippets.
- Snippet execution latency: example harness must complete <= 60s for generation examples (CI timeout 90s).
- Rollout time for critical canonical fix: <= 24 hours from triage to patch release (target).

Sample matrix (example mapping for coverage checks)

| Example type | Languages | Execution harness | Golden file location | Responsible team |
|--------------|-----------|-------------------|----------------------|------------------|
| Text generation | python, ts, go | snippets-runner v2 | /goldens/gen/<example_id>.json | SDK-language team |
| Embeddings | python, ts, java | embeddings-harness | /goldens/emb/<example_id>.json | SDK-language team |
| Streaming | python, ts | stream-sim | /goldens/stream/<example_id>.ndjson | eng-dx |
| Auth examples (curl) | curl | cli-checker | /goldens/cli/<example_id>.txt | eng-dx |

Notes: golden file names are short IDs matching doc snippet ids. The sample matrix above must be maintained in docs repo at docs/config/snippet-matrix.yaml.

CI gating: how a PR is validated

1) Lint and link-check: docs-lint pipeline (markdown, internal link checks).
2) Snippet detection: changed snippets are identified via manifest diff.
3) Execution stage: run language-specific harnesses in parallel (see 'Local validation commands' below).
4) Golden compare: harness produces output which is compared to the golden using the comparator configured per example (exact, fuzzy-text, JSON-field-equality).
5) Snapshot update policy: PRs intending to update golden outputs must include a `golden-update` label and a short rationale (regression fix, model-change, or intended API change).

Publishing gate checklist (must pass before publishing docs page)

- [ ] All changed snippets successfully executed in CI.
- [ ] Golden comparator results within configured tolerance.
- [ ] Example code build/test (where applicable) passes in nightly SDK pipelines.
- [ ] Owners reviewed and approved (reviewers list on PR).
- [ ] Telemetry contract update (if new telemetry fields are added).
- [ ] Security review (for examples that surface credentials or secret usages).

Canonical fix patterns & support playbook

Pattern A: SDK surface change (API rename/arg reorder)

1) Triage: create issue in SDK repo and docs ticket referencing doc snippet ids.
2) Patch: update SDK with backward-compatible shim if possible; otherwise publish breaking change notes.
3) Docs update: modify snippet, attach test harness output and update golden if behavior intentionally changed.
4) Notify: add support/sales slack channel notification and append to weekly release notes.

Pattern B: Runtime non-determinism (model outputs change)

1) Classify: determine if snippet is deterministic-by-design; if not, switch comparator to fuzzy-text or field-level checks.
2) Add seed / stable-mode flags to harness if model supports it.
3) If output drift breaks downstream tests, add a short-term exception and schedule an evaluation to rebaseline the golden.

Pattern C: Docs-only typo or formatting error

1) Small fix: apply patch in docs repo, run doc-lint and snippet execution.
2) Release: merge to main and follow normal docs publishing cadence.

Support canonical fixes (quick triage recipe)

- First response (within 2 business hours): confirm snippet id and environment used by customer.
- Reproduce locally using the harness and the golden. Use the exact SDK release tag reported by the customer.
- Identify whether failure is: code bug, SDK mismatch, or environment/auth issue.
- If code bug: open SDK issue, assign to oncall SDK owner, and apply a temporary docs note (inline warning) until fix is merged.

Local validation commands (developer quick reference)

# Run the snippet harness for python examples
./dev/tools/snippet-harness --lang python --example-id gen-quickstart-01 --out /tmp/out.json

# Compare output to golden (exact JSON compare)
./dev/tools/golden-compare --golden goldens/gen/gen-quickstart-01.json --actual /tmp/out.json --mode json-eq

# Run full changed-snippet set in CI-like parallel mode (Docker)
./dev/tools/runner-ci-sim --diff-from main --parallel 4 --timeout 60s

Golden example (text generation)

{
  "request": {
    "model": "redwood-alpha-1",
    "prompt": "Write a short mission statement for an inference platform",
    "temperature": 0.0
  },
  "response": {
    "text": "Redwood Inference helps engineering teams run reliable, low-latency LLM inference across hosted and private environments.",
    "tokens": 18,
    "deterministic": true
  }
}

Comparator modes (how to pick one)

- exact: use for deterministic CLI responses, auth errors, HTTP status outputs.
- json-eq: use when JSON ordering may change but field values must match.
- fuzzy-text: use when human-readable text may vary (threshold 85% token overlap default).
- ndjson-lines-eq: use for streaming outputs where line-level equivalence matters.

Rollback and hotfix procedure

1) If a docs publish introduces a critical regression (support uptick > 20% vs baseline):
   a) Revert the docs page or the PR via docs-staging rollback (one-click revert for last deploy).
   b) Flag the related SDK repo and open emergency hotfix PR.
   c) Notify support and create an incident channel for coordination.
2) Postmortem: within 72 hours, publish a short incident summary and follow-up to prevent recurrence (ownership of prevention assigned).

Observability & telemetry alignment

- Each snippet execution in CI emits a telemetry event fragment with fields: snippet_id, example_type, language, sdk_version, ci_job_id, pass/fail, comparator_mode.
- Telemetry window: retained for 90 days with dashboards in Grafana for snippet failure trends and flaky snippet lists.
- Alert: > 5 unique snippet failures in a 24-hour window fires a docs-triage PagerDuty rule to eng-dx on-call.

Appendix: Useful commands & links

- Update golden locally (developer flow):
  1) Run harness and inspect output.
  2) If change is intended, add `golden-update` label to the PR and include a short note.
  3) Attach `/goldens/<category>/<id>.json` to the PR or push to docs config.

- Common commands:
  - docs-lint: ./dev/tools/docs-lint --paths docs/pages --fix
  - snippet manifest: ./dev/tools/snippet-manifest --print-changed --base main

Related pages and references:

- docs/config/snippet-matrix.yaml (authoritative matrix)
- /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/sdk-replay-auth-testkit-and-golden-trace-2027 (replay harness design)
- /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/sdk-telemetry-contract-stability-playbook-2026 (telemetry contract)

End of document.
